claims.text: The target material is as-solidified, Co-free equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
Controlled casting can produce equiatomic FeNiCrMn with a fine grain structure.
The as-solidified FeNiCrMn matrix is BCC or otherwise single phase.
As-solidified FeNiCrMn contains a modest dispersion of nanoscale Mn-rich oxide precipitates.
Fine grains and nanoscale Mn-rich oxide precipitates control the temperature- and strain-rate-dependent mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn.
The nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion through an Orowan-type mechanism between 25 and 600 °C.
Dislocation slip and twinning are the primary deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn between 25 and 600 °C.
Precipitate strengthening is the main source of high yield strength in FeNiCrMn at low to moderate temperatures.
At temperatures of at least about 700 °C, the precipitates exert Zener drag on grain boundaries and delay full dynamic recrystallization.
Dislocation climb becomes more active in FeNiCrMn at temperatures of at least about 700 °C.
The combined Orowan strengthening and delayed recrystallization sustain a favorable strength-ductility balance over a wide temperature and strain-rate range.
FeNiCrMn undergoes a measurable change in strain hardening and flow stress associated with partial dynamic recrystallization above about 700 °C.
Increasing precipitate volume fraction will systematically increase the dynamic yield strength of FeNiCrMn.
Refining the grains will systematically increase the dynamic yield strength of FeNiCrMn.
Increasing precipitate volume fraction or refining grains will delay dynamic recrystallization relative to the baseline.
Coarsening the grains or reducing precipitate volume fraction will lower dynamic yield strength and promote earlier recrystallization.
Systematic variation of cooling rate can generate specimens having different grain sizes and precipitate volume fractions.
The cited CoCrFeMnNi study demonstrates temperature-dependent yield strength in a related equiatomic alloy, including retention of comparatively high strength through 700 °C.
